name: Websites
label: A home for your business
title:
Your next chapter.
On the web.
description: Build a website with AI using Atomic. Describe your business, shape the design on the canvas, and publish when you are ready.
intro: Give your business a place that feels like you. Describe the site you have in mind, shape every detail on the canvas, and turn visitors into your next conversation.
summary: A portfolio, a business site, a landing page. Make a first impression that feels like you.
benefit_title: A website with your point of view.
benefit_intro: Start with your story. Make the layout, the content, and the next step work around it.
benefits: Make your own first impression
Describe your style or upload a visual reference. Refine typography, colour, and layout on the canvas.
Give every page a purpose
Introduce your work, explain your services, and help visitors find the right way to get in touch.
Keep the next update simple
Edit text in place or ask for a new section. Preview and check the result before publishing your changes.
prompts: Studio portfolio
Build an architecture studio website with selected projects, large photographs, our approach, and a contact page.
Business website
Create a consultancy website with our services, team biographies, frequently asked questions, and a contact form.
Launch landing page
Design a landing page for a new coffee subscription with a product story, plan comparison, and an interest form.
workflow: Tell Atomic who you are, what pages you need, and what visitors should do next.
Add your own words and images, adjust the design, and try the site at different screen sizes.
Run the build checks, publish your verified site, and connect a custom domain on a paid plan.
faqs: Can I start without knowing how to code?

Yes. Describe the pages and style you want in plain language. Use the canvas to refine the generated screens, then review and test the site before publishing. You can also inspect and download the source.
Can I use my own images and design references?
Yes. Atomic supports image uploads and design references. Bring your own photography and brand materials, then use the canvas controls and conversation to refine the result.
Can I publish on my own domain?
Atomic supports publishing on an Atomic subdomain. Custom domains are included in the proposed paid plans; you register the domain separately. See the publishing guide for setup and verification.
Can my website collect enquiries?

You can build an enquiry workflow with an app backend. Persistent data and user authentication are included for one app on the proposed Free plan, and for every app on Builder and Pro. Review the plan details and test how your forms store and handle enquiries.

name: Online stores
label: From your shelf to their screen
title:
A little shop.
All your own.
description: Create an online storefront with Atomic: product collections, a shopping cart, customer accounts, and an order management workflow shaped around your shop.
intro: Put your products in the spotlight. Build a storefront with room for your story, a cart for your customers, and an order view that makes sense to you.
summary: Bring your products, collections, and orders together in a storefront with personality.
benefit_title: Your products deserve their own space.
benefit_intro: Build around what you sell and how you work, from the first collection to the next order.
benefits: Let the collection lead
Give products their own images, descriptions, and categories. Shape the storefront around your brand.
Think beyond the product page
Start from the Storefront template for a catalogue, cart, checkout flow, order history, and shop manager.
Build for both sides of the counter
Preview the customer and admin roles. Check which records each can see before you welcome real customers.
prompts: Independent maker
Build a ceramics storefront with product collections, detailed product pages, a cart, and an owner view for managing orders.
Small retail shop
Create a plant shop with indoor and outdoor categories, care information, a shopping cart, and customer order history.
Seasonal collection
Make a storefront for a limited stationery collection with product photography, gift sets, and an order management screen.
workflow: Describe your products and order process, or begin with the Storefront template.
Replace sample products and images, try the cart, and review the customer and shop-manager screens.
Verify your order flow and app permissions before publishing. Configure and test a payment provider separately if you need online payments.
faqs: Is there a storefront template?

Yes. Atomic’s Storefront template includes a product catalogue, categories, cart and checkout screens, order history, and a shop-manager view. It opens with sample data so you can explore the flow before making it your own.
Does a checkout screen mean I can accept live payments?

No. An order or checkout flow is separate from payment processing. Taking money requires a payment provider, the appropriate integration, and end-to-end testing. Atomic does not promise a ready-made payment integration here.
Can customers have accounts and order history?

Yes, these are part of the Storefront template. The proposed Free plan includes a backend, database, and authentication for one app; Builder and Pro include them for every app. Test customer access to order records before publishing.
What should I replace before launch?
Replace placeholder text and images, remove sample products and records, and verify access rules for customer and staff data. Preview accounts are for testing and are not published with your app.

name: Booking apps
label: Make room for your next client
title:
Less back and forth.
More booked in.
description: Build a booking app with Atomic. Give clients a way to choose a service and request a time, with staff and owner views to manage the day.
intro: Give clients a clear path from choosing a service to finding a time. Bring bookings, staff, and your day’s work into an app made around your business.
summary: Help clients choose a service and find a time. Give your team a clearer view of the day.
benefit_title: A better flow, for everyone’s day.
benefit_intro: Think through the whole appointment: what clients choose, what staff see, and what the owner manages.
benefits: Put your services up front
Organise services, durations, staff, and opening hours. Start from the Salon Booking template and adapt it to your business.
Make the day easier to read
Give staff a day view and owners a dashboard. Shape the screens around how your team handles bookings.
Try the complete journey
Preview as a customer, staff member, or owner. Test the booking and management flow before publishing.
prompts: Salon appointments
Build a salon booking app with services, stylists, opening hours, customer bookings, a staff day view, and an owner dashboard.
Creative consultations
Create a consultation booking app for a design studio with service options, available times, and an owner view to manage requests.
Workshop bookings
Make a pottery workshop booking app with class details, session dates, participant sign-up, and an organiser view.
workflow: Explain your services, who takes bookings, and how a client chooses a time.
Try the customer and team screens with sample bookings. Adjust the flow and check availability rules.
Replace sample records, verify access and booking behaviour, then publish the app for your clients.
faqs: Can I begin with a booking template?
Yes. The Salon Booking template brings services, stylists, opening hours, booking screens, a staff day view, and an owner dashboard. Explore it with sample data, then adapt the app to your business.
Can I test the experience as different people?
Yes. Use the role preview to see the app as a customer, staff member, or owner. The sample account for each role helps you check its screens and records.
Will this connect to my existing calendar or send reminders?

These pages do not promise calendar integrations or automated reminders. Include those requirements in your brief and confirm how the integration will work. Test any external service before relying on it.
Which plan supports real bookings?

Persistent booking data and user sign-in require a backend, included in the proposed Builder and Pro plans. Free supports frontend exploration. Review the launch plans and test data access and booking behaviour before going live.

name: Client portals
label: A shared place to move things forward
title:
Keep your clients
in the picture.
description: Create a client portal with Atomic for project updates, milestones, and requests. Design client and team views and test who can access each record.
intro: Give every project a home beyond the email thread. Build a place where clients can check progress, see what is next, and keep the conversation moving.
summary: Give projects, milestones, and client requests a home beyond the email thread.
benefit_intro: A useful portal starts with a simple question: what does your client need to know or do next?
benefits: Make progress visible
Design a project overview with milestones, status, and next steps that your clients can understand at a glance.
Make the next step clear
Add screens for client requests and project updates. Describe the records and actions your workflow needs.
Design each person’s view
Define client and team roles, then preview each one. Verify access to project records before inviting clients.
prompts: Agency client workspace
Build a client portal for a design agency with project milestones, status updates, client requests, and separate client and team views.
Consulting projects
Create a consultancy portal where clients can see engagement progress and next steps, and consultants can manage project updates.
Architecture project hub
Make a portal for an architecture studio with project phases, meeting notes, decisions, and a client-specific project overview.
workflow: Describe what clients should see, what your team manages, and which records belong to each project.
Refine the dashboard and preview both sides. Check that each role sees the right project and actions.
Test access with separate accounts and real backend records, remove sample data, and publish when the checks pass.
faqs: Can each client see only their own projects?

That is an access rule to include in your brief and verify in the finished app. Atomic’s backend supports identity and permissions, but a role preview alone is not proof of isolation. Test with separate accounts and records before inviting clients.
Can the team and clients have different views?
Yes. Describe the screens and actions for each role. Atomic supports screen and role previews so you can try the workflow as different people while you build.
Do I need a paid plan for client accounts?
The proposed Free plan includes the backend, database, and authentication a portal needs for one app; Builder and Pro include them for every app, along with collaboration.
Can I keep the generated code?
Yes. You can browse and download the generated source. A source download does not include client accounts, business records, or hosting. Plan any data migration separately.

name: Internal tools
label: Built around the way you work
title:
Your workflow.
With a better view.
description: Build internal tools with Atomic: CRMs, help desks, request trackers, and team dashboards. Start with your workflow and refine the app with your team.
intro: Turn the process your team knows by heart into a tool everyone can use. Track the work, give each person the right view, and make the next action easier to find.
summary: A CRM, a help desk, a request tracker. Build around the process your team actually uses.
benefit_title: Give a familiar process a useful home.
benefit_intro: Start with one workflow. Make the records, stages, and responsibilities clear before adding more.
benefits: Start with the work
Describe the records you track and the stages they move through. Use Pipeline CRM or Help Desk as a starting point.
Build the view each role needs
Give sales, support, and admins screens for their own work. Preview roles and check who can read and change records.
Refine with your team
Use shared workspaces and app collaborators on paid plans. Review changes together and keep a verified source version to return to.
prompts: Sales pipeline
Build a CRM for a small agency with companies, contacts, deals by stage, an activity log, and a sales dashboard.
Team help desk
Create an internal help desk with request submission, an agent queue, internal notes, and a knowledge base.
Request tracker
Make a team request tracker with categories, assignees, statuses, and separate requester and manager views.
workflow: Outline one process: the records, the stages, and who owns each action.
Try the tool with sample records and each team role. Refine the screens and test changes before applying them.
Verify record access, replace test data, and publish. Invite the right people to use and maintain the app.
faqs: What templates are available for teams?

Pipeline CRM includes companies, contacts, staged deals, an activity log, and a dashboard. Help Desk includes requests, an agent queue, internal notes, and a knowledge base. Both are documented starting points you can adapt.
Can colleagues help build the app?

Yes. Shared workspaces and invited app collaborators are included in the proposed paid plans, with Editor and Admin roles. These building permissions are separate from the roles of people using your finished app.
Can I connect an existing business system?

Include the system and the required data flow in your brief. A connection needs a supported API, credentials, and implementation and testing. These pages do not promise ready-made integrations or automatic spreadsheet imports.
Can I restore a previous version?

Atomic supports verified source history and frontend rollback. Restoring source or rolling back a published frontend does not restore business data. Plan data recovery separately and review the versioning guide.

name: Prototypes
label: Make the idea something you can try
title:
Show the idea.
Find the next step.
description: Turn a product idea into a testable prototype with Atomic. Explore screens, preview user roles, collect feedback, and refine the experience on the canvas.
intro: Move the conversation beyond a description. Build screens people can try, explore the flow together, and use what you learn to decide what comes next.
summary: Put a testable idea in front of people. Learn from the flow before expanding the scope.
benefit_title: Give your next conversation something to work with.
benefit_intro: A focused prototype helps you test a useful question instead of trying to build everything at once.
benefits: Start with one useful journey
Describe who the app is for and the action you want to test. Build the screens that support that path first.
See more than the happy path
Explore screens, roles, and dialog states on the canvas. Try the experience with sample data before connecting real users.
Turn feedback into a revision
Point to an element, add a visual annotation, and ask for a change. Keep source versions as the idea develops.
prompts: Community events
Prototype a community events app with an event list, event details, an RSVP flow, and an organiser’s attendee view.
Product onboarding
Build a prototype for a project planning app with a welcome screen, project setup, first task, and a simple team dashboard.
Client concept
Create a prototype of a membership portal with a member home, resource library, and an admin view using sample content.
workflow: Choose the question you want to answer and describe the smallest journey that can test it.
Try the screens and states, gather feedback, and use the canvas and annotations to refine the idea.
Share a published frontend when appropriate. Add a backend on a paid plan when you are ready to test persistent data and real accounts.
faqs: Is a prototype a finished production app?

No. A prototype helps you explore a design and workflow. Before a real launch, review the generated code, test behaviour and access rules, replace sample content, and check any integrations and data handling.
Can I start with a frontend only?

Yes. Your screens start on sample data, with visual editing, source history, and source downloads. The proposed Free plan adds a backend, database, and authentication for one app; Builder and Pro add them for every app, with collaboration.
Can I try different roles and dialog states?
Yes. Atomic’s canvas supports screen and role previews, including states such as open dialogs. Templates bring sample accounts and records so you can explore a workflow from different perspectives.
Can a developer continue from my prototype?

You can inspect and download the generated source to review or hand off. Downloads do not include app users, business data, or hosting infrastructure. Broader app packaging and deployment choices remain on the roadmap.
